title: Cache hit-rate dashboard mock (KV/prefix cache telemetry v2) — panel list + query notes
content:
Context
- This is an early mock of the cache hit-rate dashboards we want to ship with KV/prefix cache telemetry v2.
- Intended consumers: Runtime, SRE, Optimize, Support.
- Goals:
  1) Make cache effectiveness trustworthy (hit/miss/partial) and comparable across routes/models/regions.
  2) Let us explain the “why”: cacheable prompt ratio, fragmentation, evictions, and savings.
  3) Keep drilldowns useful without blowing up cardinality.

Assumptions / working vocabulary
- Cache = prefix/KV cache used during prefill (and partially during decode depending on runtime).
- “Hit” means prefix tokens found in cache and reused (no prefill compute for those tokens).
- “Partial” means some prefix tokens hit, some miss (common when prompt has stable system prefix but variable early user content).
- “Cacheable prompt ratio” is a proxy for: of incoming prompts, how many have a prefix long enough / stable enough to benefit.

Telemetry v2 fields assumed (names are placeholders until spec is finalized)
- Counters:
  - kv_cache.lookup_total
  - kv_cache.lookup_hit_total
  - kv_cache.lookup_partial_total
  - kv_cache.lookup_miss_total
  - kv_cache.insert_total
  - kv_cache.evict_total
- Token/bytes accounting:
  - kv_cache.hit_tokens_total
  - kv_cache.hit_bytes_total
  - kv_cache.request_tokens_total (prefill tokens seen)
- Time savings:
  - kv_cache.saved_prefill_ms_total
- Gauges / capacity (optional, if runtime exports):
  - kv_cache.resident_bytes
  - kv_cache.resident_entries
- Required tags for attribution (subject to ADR/cardinality budget):
  - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise) OR tenant_bucket (hashed)
  - deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
  - region
  - route_id (normalized)
  - model_id (normalized)
  - model_version (coarse / pinned alias, not per-build hash)
  - cache_policy (policy name)

Cardinality constraints (notes)
- Avoid raw tenant_id / request_id on metrics. If we need per-tenant, do it in logs/traces or via hashed bucket (N=128/256) with sampling.
- route_id, model_id, region are allowed; model_version may need to be coarsened (“stable”, “canary”, “pinned”) depending on explosion.
- For “top offenders” views, use pre-aggregated datasets or query-time topk with strict limits.

Dashboard set (mock)

Dashboard A: Cache effectiveness overview (global + by deployment_mode)

A1) Global hit-rate (time series)
- What: hit rate across all traffic.
- Definition:
  - hit_rate = hit_tokens_total / request_tokens_total
  - alternative: lookup_hit_total / lookup_total (less aligned to savings if token lengths vary)
- Query sketch (PromQL-ish):
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_tokens_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_request_tokens_total[5m]))
- Slice controls: deployment_mode, region.
- Notes:
  - Must clearly label which denominator we use (tokens-based strongly preferred).
  - If request_tokens_total isn’t present, we can use (hit_tokens + miss_tokens) if runtime exports miss_tokens_total.

A2) Hit / partial / miss breakdown (stacked area)
- What: share of requests by outcome.
- Definition:
  - request_outcome_rate = outcome_requests / total_requests
- Query sketch:
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_hit_total[5m])) by (deployment_mode) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_total[5m])) by (deployment_mode)
  - same for partial/miss.
- Data gap risk:
  - Outcome classification has known edge cases (streaming retries, partial-prefill) → need runtime known-issues list surfaced.

A3) Saved prefill time (saved_prefill_ms) (time series + cumulative)
- What: estimated GPU/CPU prefill compute saved.
- Query sketch:
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_saved_prefill_ms_total[5m]))
- Companion ratio (efficiency):
  - saved_ms_per_1k_tokens = (rate(saved_prefill_ms_total) / rate(request_tokens_total)) * 1000
- Notes:
  - Saved_prefill_ms must be computed in runtime (or gateway) consistently; otherwise it will drift and mislead.

A4) Hit-bytes (time series)
- What: bytes reused from cache (proxy for memory bandwidth/compute avoided).
- Query sketch:
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_bytes_total[5m]))
- Notes:
  - Ensure bytes definition is stable across quantization profiles (FP16 vs INT8 changes KV footprint).

A5) Cacheable prompt ratio (time series)
- What: fraction of requests eligible to benefit (enough prefix length, cache enabled, no disqualifying flags).
- Proposed definition (v0):
  - cacheable_ratio = cacheable_requests / total_requests
  - cacheable_requests criteria (runtime): prompt_prefix_tokens >= MIN_PREFIX && cache_policy != "disabled" && not streaming_retry
- Query sketch:
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_cacheable_requests_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- Data gap:
  - cacheable_requests_total does not exist today; needs runtime classification or gateway enrichment.

Dashboard B: Drilldowns (route/model/region)

B1) Hit-rate by route_id (top 20)
- What: which routes benefit (or regress).
- Query sketch:
  - topk(20, (sum(rate(hit_tokens_total[10m])) by (route_id)) / (sum(rate(request_tokens_total[10m])) by (route_id)))
- Controls: filter by deployment_mode, region, model_id.
- Notes:
  - route_id normalization is critical (avoid cardinality from dynamic route params).
  - For private deployments, route_id may be missing; define fallback (route="unknown").

B2) Hit-rate by model_id (top 20)
- What: identify model-specific differences (tokenization/prefix stability).
- Query sketch:
  - topk(20, hit_rate by model_id)
- Notes:
  - Some traffic uses model routing (aliases). We need both requested_model and served_model, but not both on every metric if too high cardinality.

B3) Hit-rate by (route_id, model_id) heatmap
- What: detect fragmentation and mismatches where route pins multiple model versions.
- Query sketch:
  - hit_rate grouped by route_id,model_id; display as heatmap.
- Cardinality warning:
  - route_id x model_id can explode; restrict to top routes by volume, or pre-aggregate daily dataset.

B4) “Fragmentation index” (proposal)
- What: a single signal that a route is spread across many model_versions or regions (bad for cache locality).
- Options:
  - entropy(route → model_version distribution)
  - unique(model_version) per route over 1h window
- Data gap:
  - We don’t have a stable model_version tag yet that doesn’t explode (needs ADR decision).

Dashboard C: Cache health (evictions, residency, policy)

C1) Evictions rate by cache_policy
- What: high evictions can reduce hit-rate (thrash).
- Query sketch:
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_evict_total[5m])) by (cache_policy, deployment_mode)
- Notes:
  - Interpret with resident_bytes if available; otherwise evictions alone are ambiguous.

C2) Inserts vs lookups (ratio)
- What: if inserts are low but misses are high, something’s wrong (cache disabled/misconfigured).
- Query sketch:
  - sum(rate(insert_total[5m])) / sum(rate(lookup_total[5m]))
- Data gap:
  - Some runtimes may not emit insert_total on all paths (e.g., if admission control drops inserts); need a counter for “insert_skipped_reason”.

C3) Resident bytes / entries (if exported)
- What: detect saturation / undersizing and correlate to evictions.
- Query sketch:
  - avg_over_time(kv_cache_resident_bytes[5m]) by (deployment_mode, region)
- Notes:
  - If not exported, we might approximate via internal runtime stats endpoint + scrape.

C4) Policy compliance / mismatches
- What: show when requests are tagged with a cache_policy but runtime behaves differently (e.g., policy disabled at runtime).
- Proposal:
  - metric: kv_cache.policy_applied_total{policy="X"}
  - metric: kv_cache.policy_mismatch_total{reason=...}
- Data gap:
  - Not currently planned; might be v2.1 depending on runtime effort.

Dashboard D: Debug / data quality (internal-only)

D1) Metric coverage: % of requests with cache tags present
- What: detect missing attribution tags (route/model/region/deployment_mode).
- Query sketch:
  - (sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{route_id!=""}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])))
  - replicate for model_id, region.
- Notes:
  - This is the fastest way to catch gateway rollout issues.

D2) Cardinality watch panel
- What: number of active series for cache metrics.
- Query sketch:
  - count(count_over_time({__name__=~"kv_cache_.*"}[10m])) by (__name__)
- Notes:
  - Add threshold annotations aligned with ADR budget.

D3) Sampling rate confirmation
- What: verify sampling is applied as intended per tier/region.
- Proposal:
  - metric: kv_cache.sampled_requests_total
  - metric: kv_cache.requests_total
  - derived: sampled_ratio
- Data gap:
  - We need explicit sampled indicator. Without it, drops in traffic could be mistaken for sampling changes.

Open questions (for Logan/Nadia/Caleb)
1) Canonical hit-rate definition: tokens-based vs lookup-based. I think tokens-based should be primary; lookup-based as supporting panel.
2) Partial hits: do we report partial as a separate numerator for “effective_hit_rate” (hit_tokens + partial_hit_tokens) / request_tokens? Needs clarity.
3) Denominator for request_tokens_total: prefill-only tokens or total tokens (prefill + decode)? For caching, prefill-only is more honest.
4) Model/version tagging:
   - How do we represent served model vs requested model without cardinality blowup?
   - Can we use model_alias (stable) plus model_build (only in traces/logs)?
5) Tenant segmentation:
   - For SRE: tier is enough.
   - For Optimize: we need per-tenant recommendations; likely via offline dataset keyed by tenant_id (not high-cardinality metrics).

Known data gaps / blockers (as of 2025-02-14)
- saved_prefill_ms_total not implemented everywhere; runtime PR pending.
- hit_bytes_total depends on a consistent KV footprint calculation across quantization; needs spec to define.
- cacheable_requests_total not yet defined; we need a runtime-side classifier.
- route_id normalization in gateway is incomplete; dynamic params are currently leaking (cardinality risk).
- Private deployments: region/deployment_mode tagging inconsistent; require a fallback scheme and explicit “unknown”.
- Partial-prefill and streaming retry misclassification suspected (see runtime debug thread); dashboards must carry a warning banner until fixed.

Next steps
- Sergio: convert this mock into observability-pack dashboard JSON draft (with placeholders) once metric names are finalized.
- Nadia/Caleb: confirm which fields will exist at ingest (metric tags vs log attributes) and what we can query in near-real-time.
- Logan: finalize v2 spec mapping for these panels (names + units + tags) and confirm cardinality-safe groupings.
- Mei: draft a companion “dashboard interpretation guide” (one-pager) for Support/Optimize (what does it mean when hit-rate is high but savings is low, etc.).

Appendix: panel naming conventions (draft)
- Use “KV cache” in titles (not “prefix cache”) unless we split prefix vs KV later.
- Always include denominator in subtitles (tokens-based vs requests-based).
- Put deployment_mode and region as first-class template variables on every dashboard.
